THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 10.11.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.371/2015, ON THE FILE OF THE JUDGE, ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES AND SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MYSURU, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT MFA No.779/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on the ground that the driver of the goods auto was not rash and negligent but the deceased herself had come to the wrong side of the road.
Therefore, the deceased was entirely responsible for the accident and challenging on the quantum of compensation.
2. MFA No.4623/2018 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation as monthly salary of the deceased was taken on the lesser side which is contrary to the evidence on record.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 13.08.2014 at about 3.15 p.m., the deceased-Chandrakala was riding her TVS Scooty bearing No.KA-09-EC-6160 near Preethi Granite Factory Road of Hebbal Industrial Area, at that time, a goods auto bearing No.KA-45-5332 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner from opposite side and dashed against the TVS Scooty.
Due to impact, the deceased succumbed to the injuries.

Therefore, the claimants have preferred to file claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short).
4.
Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
REGARDING RASH AND NEGLIGENT ASPECT:
5. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the deceased was entirely responsible to the accident as she has driven her two wheeler towards the wrong side of the road.

Further, it is submitted that the driver of the auto rickshaw was coming on his correct side and if the deceased had proceeded on her correct side then the accident would not have been occurred but the deceased had taken her two wheeler towards the wrong side of the road and hit the auto rickshaw and fell Puttaraju vs Manjunatha J on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80576998/
4 down herself and succumbed to the injuries and therefore, with reference to the spot mahazar and spot sketch, learned counsel argued that which clearly shows that the deceased was entirely rash and negligent in driving the two wheeler and caused accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal has wrongly appreciated the evidence on record and without evaluating the evidence found that the deceased was completely rash and negligent and thus the accident was caused.
Therefore, prays to set aside the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
Further, it is submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

Further, it is submitted that the claimants themselves in their claim petition and in their evidence stated that the deceased was receiving salary of Rs.10,000/- p.m. and that is accordingly considered and granted compensation.
Therefore, it is submitted that even otherwise the compensation amount may not be held as on higher side but awarded just compensation.
Therefore, prays at least to hold contributory negligence on part of the deceased as it is proved from the spot mahazar and spot sketch.

Further, it is submitted that just because the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the auto rickshaw that alone cannot be made as a ground to say that the driver of the auto rickshaw was completely rash and negligent.

Therefore,
prays to re-appreciate the evidence on record.
Hence, prays to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant submitted that the deceased had not taken two wheeler on the wrong side of the road, but was riding the vehicle on her correct side, but the autorickshaw had come to wrong side of the road and hit the claimant and this is clearly established in the police records.
Further more, there is no contra evidence on behalf of the Insurance Company to prove that the autorickshaw was not rash and negligent.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in evaluating the evidence on record and correctly came to the conclusion that the driver of the autorickshaw was rash and negligent in driving the autorickshaw.
Further submitted that the compensation amount awarded is on the lesser side.
Therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation.
7. In the present case, the factum of accident between the deceased who was riding her TVS scooty and goods auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-45-5332 is not disputed.
The death of the deceased in the accident is not disputed.

The disputed fact is that whether the deceased has also made her contributory negligence to the accident or whether the driver of the auto rickshaw was completely rash and negligent in driving the auto rickshaw and caused accident.
The Tribunal held that the driver of the auto rickshaw was completely rash and negligent in driving the auto rickshaw.
Therefore, fastened the entire negligence on part of the driver of the auto rickshaw.
Upon giving finding, the Tribunal has not discussed the evidence tendered regarding rash and negligent aspect.
The Tribunal has stated that such and such documents are produced but there is no discussion and appreciation of materials revealed in the evidence.
The Tribunal assigned the reason that none of the parties have challenged the FIR and charge sheet and much less the Insurance Company has not challenged the FIR and charge sheet.
Therefore, on these reasons held that the driver of the auto rickshaw was rash and negligent.

sentences.text: Upon the base of complaint lodged, the criminal law was set into motion culminating into filing of the charge sheet against the driver of the auto rickshaw but filing of the charge sheet only against the driver of the goods auto rickshaw is not a conclusive proof so as to say that the driver of the auto rickshaw was completely rash and negligent.
The Tribunal and this Court on the appeal has to evaluate and assess the evidences independently to find out the rash and negligent aspect.

The acquittal or conviction of the accused of offences of rash and negligent driving does not have any impact on the assessment of rash and negligent aspect to be made by the Tribunal in the claim proceedings.
The evidence tendered before the Tribunal in the claim proceedings ought to be examined independently on the theory of preponderance of probability.

In criminal case, the guilt of the accused of the offences of rash and negligent act/driving is to be assessed and evaluated on the touch-stone of proof "beyond reasonable doubt", but in the claim proceedings, the evidences ought to be appreciated regarding the rash - 11 - and negligent driving of the drivers but not the offence.
Therefore, the degree of appreciation of evidence in criminal cases and in motor vehicles accident claim proceedings are entirely two different aspects.
Even though there is no requirement of strict Rules of pleadings and evidence in considering the claim petition arising out of motor vehicles accident cases.
But, the theory of preponderance of probability means upon evidence produced before the Tribunal/Court what would get impression in the mind regarding occurrence of incident is to be assessed.
But in criminal cases whether the named accused is guilty or not is to be assessed.
This is difference between the appreciation of evidence so far as rash and negligent aspect is concerned in both these category of cases.

Even though basically in both proceedings, the fundamental aspect regarding finding of rash and negligent aspect but in criminal cases, strictly it is to be tested and held whether the accused is guilty of offence of rash and negligent driving/act but in claim proceedings, whether due to rash and negligent driving/act, the - 12 - accident was caused or not is to be considered.
This makes difference in both these cases as it is vogue in considering the cases of these two type of categories.
9. Therefore, on the above said principle, the evidence in the present case is to be appreciated on its preponderance of probability.
10. Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that there is no concept of any contributory negligence in MV Act.
He has referred Section 166 of the MV Act.

But this argument cannot be accepted for the reason that where claim petition is filed under Section 166 of MV Act, one of the aspect to be considered is whether the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, where one of the prime aspect is to consider the rash and negligent aspect, the entirety of rash and negligence or contributory or composite negligence can be considered.

Where the claim petition is filed under Section 166 of MV Act, the decision to be taken on rash and negligent driving of the offending Puttaraju vs Manjunatha J on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80576998/
6 - 13 - motor vehicle is to be considered as this is sine quo non for determining the claim petitions.
11. Therefore, in catena of decisions, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has pronounced that when the claim petition is filed under Section 166 of MV Act, the rash and negligent aspect is to be considered.
The secondary aspect is whether the rash and negligent aspect is wholly on the driver of the offending vehicle named in the police record or partial or contributory or composite.

Therefore,
when the claim petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, the rash and negligent aspect is to be considered in its entirety.
Whether there is any apportionment of rash and negligent aspect on the driver of two vehicles, on this basis, the theory of contributory negligence and composite negligence is resolved.
Section 165 of Motor Vehicle Act stipulates constitution of Claim Tribunal and an application is to be filed before the Claim Tribunal.
But how the claim petition is to be adjudicated is covered by the provision of Section 166 and Section 168 - 14 - of Motor Vehicle Act.
Therefore, in this way, the application filed as in the present case is also the claim arising out of Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, then the rash and negligent aspect is also to be considered.
12. The rash and negligent aspect is to be considered on the basis of evidence produced before the Tribunal/Court by the parties and the same has to be appreciated.

The Tribunal while giving this finding on the theory of preponderance of probabilities as arraigned of parties is not the factual truth to hold that the charge sheeted driver always and alone is responsible for the accident where the theory beyond reasonable doubt is not applicable and where the case is to be considered on the theory of preponderance of probabilities.

The human mind gets impression as to whether the accident or incident has happened or not and who is responsible and to what extent, without going in depth in considering the evidence applying any strict rules.

Based upon the evidence produced before the Tribunal what is emerged to get - 15 - impression about occurrence of incident or accident and to what proportion the persons are responsible is the preponderance of probabilities.
The application of strict rules of evidence and theory of beyond reasonable doubt is applicable where a person is prosecuted for guilty of certain offence.
Considering the guilty of offence and responsible in causing incident or accident is different.

In the claim proceedings, the Tribunal/Court is not an obligation to find the guilty of a person for commission of offence rather the claim petition ought to be considered on the theory of preponderance of probabilities to get impression as to what must have been occurred upon the impression got by the evidence on record.
Therefore, the theory of preponderance of probabilities is applicable to ascertain whether any incident or accident has occurred or not and who is responsible and to what extent.
Therefore, on this principle, the claim petitions ought to be considered.

sentences.text: In the present case, P.W.1 is the husband of deceased has lodged the complaint before the police.
He alleged that the driver of the autorickshaw was coming with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
Based on that, FIR was registered and investigation was carried out culminating into filing of charge sheet.
But at the same time, P.W.1 who is the husband of the deceased had stated that the police have conducted the spot panchanama and prepared the spot sketch besides recording the statement.
Ex.P.3 is spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 is the spot sketch.
P.W.1 in his evidence has admitted that according to his instruction the police have conducted the spot panchanama and prepared the spot sketch.
What is the spot mahazar conducted and spot sketch prepared that are done by the police as per the showing place of accident as true.

Therefore,
in the present case, the spot mahazar and spot sketch are prepared at the instance of P.W.1.
The place of accident is shown in the spot mahazar and spot sketch and accordingly they are prepared.
Then the evidence of P.W.1 - 17 - gets importance to consider on the rash and negligent aspect.
As per these documents, the road is in the direction of East to West.
The autorickshaw was coming in the direction of East to West and the deceased was riding her TVS Scooty from West to East.
Admittedly, both the vehicles were moving in the opposite direction.
Therefore, it is expected on the part of both the drivers to proceed on their direction without crossing middle of the road.
The place of accident is considered as per spot mahazar and spot sketch as the said place of accident is shown by P.W.1 as admitted in the cross-examination.
Then it is revealed from these two documentary evidences that the place of accident is 11 feet away from North edge of the road and 9 feet away from South edge of the road.
Width of the road is 20 feet.
Therefore, the deceased has driven her TVS Scooty towards wrong side of the road.

The autorickshaw was coming from East to West and was on its own direction and the deceased has driven by taking her TVS Scooty towards the right side turn, which is the wrong side and intercepted the way of autorickshaw.
In - 18 - this way, the accident was caused.
Therefore, the deceased had crossed the permitted area of 10 feet from Northern side and moved towards the wrong side and intercepted the way of autorickshaw.
In this way, the accident was caused.

Therefore, when upon these evidences are considered on the basis of principle of res ipsa loquitor (things speaks itself), it is found that the deceased has also contributed her negligence to the accident.
It cannot be said that the driver of the autorickshaw was not at all rash and negligent.
If the driver of the autorickshaw had seen the deceased was coming on the wrong side and the driver of the autorickshaw could have slowed down the speed of the vehicle

,
then the accident would have been avoided.
Therefore, these factors are considered and there is contributory negligence on the part of both the drivers of the vehicles.
Therefore, it is proved that the deceased while riding TVS Scooty and the driver of the autorickshaw both have contributed rashness and negligence while causing the accident.

sentences.text: By relying on the said judgement, the learned counsel upon highlighting the observations made at paragraph No.23 regarding spot sketch and the place and spot of accident cannot be ascertained.

In the above stated judgement, wherein at paragraph No.23, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in the facts and circumstances that after the accident the motorcycle was removed and placed by the side of the road and in that spot sketch that is shown as spot of accident.

Therefore, in that case, it is emerged that the place of accident was shown and after the accident, the motorcycle was removed and placed by the side of the road and therefore, AIR 2018 SC 1900 - 20 - with these observations, after the accident the motorcycle was removed and parked is not the place of accident.
Therefore, in that context, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has disbelieved the spot sketch by observing at paragraph No.23.
But in the present case, the facts in this regard are different.
In the present case, the place and spot of accident is not the place where either the autorickshaw or TVS Scooty was removed and placed, but it is the spot of accident shown by P.W.1 himself.

Therefore,
when P.W.1 has shown the spot of accident and the police have conducted the spot panchanama and spot sketch by mentioning the distance and direction as enumerated therein and as discussed above,
the spot of accident is on the wrong side direction of the road, in which direction, the deceased was going.
Therefore, in this way, the place of accident is proved.

Upon this different factual matrix in the above stated judgement and in the present case, the above said judgment is not applicable in the present case while appreciating the evidence on record on its preponderance of probabilities.

Therefore, whether it is - 21 - proved that the deceased has also contributed negligence towards the accident and also the driver of the autorickshaw had also contributed negligence and where it is found that both are responsible,
then 25% of contributory negligence can be attributed on the part of the deceased and 75% can be attributed on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
16. The Tribunal has not at all considered and discussed and appreciated the evidence of these documents.
Simply recording the documents and without making discussion on it and coming to the conclusion is not an application of mind.

An application of mind while appreciating the evidence on record is to referring and considering the documents and discussion on the contents therein along with oral evidence and application of mind is an appreciation of evidence on its touchstone on the principle as above discussed.

Therefore, in this regard, the Tribunal has committed error in giving finding on Issue No.1 and it is modified by holding that the deceased - 22 - Puttaraju vs Manjunatha J on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80576998/

of his rashness and negligence to the accident.
Accordingly, it is modified.

The claimants are husband, children and father of the deceased.
The deceased was working as a security - 23 - guard.
The Tribunal had considered the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,619/-.

Even though, P.W.1 had stated in the claim petition that the monthly income of the deceased is Rs.10,000/-, but the documentary evidence of wage register maintained by the employer as per Ex.P.21 to Ex.P.28 shows that the salary of the deceased was Rs.7,430/-, but P.W.2 who is the office manager of the security bureau in his cross-examination has given answer to the questions put by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that as per Ex.P.20 the basic wage of the deceased was Rs.7,430/-.
Ex.P.14-bank pass book proves that the bank account of the deceased raised from Rs.9,948/- to Rs.10,395/- was being credited apart from basic wage.
The Company has also given other emoluments certainly crossed the salary of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Therefore, by considering all these evidences as the deceased was working as a security guard in Mysore city, then certainly the deceased was receiving income of Rs.10,000/- per month as held by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has committed error in deducting 1/3rd of amount towards personal and living expenses.
The claimants are husband, children and father of the deceased.
It cannot be said that the father of the deceased is not depending on the deceased.
When at an advanced age, if any person loses his wife and if there are no male children, then ultimately father of the married women has to live along with the daughter's family.
Therefore, there are totally four dependents, hence, 1/4th is deducted towards personal and living expenses.
The deceased was aged 42 years, therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable is 14.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2, 25% of income is to be added towards future prospects in life.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. In the present case, the factum of accident between the deceased who was riding her TVS scooty and goods auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-45-5332 is not disputed.
The disputed fact is that whether the deceased has also made her contributory negligence to the accident or whether the driver of the auto rickshaw was completely rash and negligent in driving the auto rickshaw and caused accident.
Therefore, on these reasons held that the driver of the auto rickshaw was rash and negligent.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The acquittal or conviction of the accused of offences of rash and negligent driving does not have any impact on the assessment of rash and negligent aspect to be made by the Tribunal in the claim proceedings.
The evidence tendered before the Tribunal in the claim proceedings ought to be examined independently on the theory of preponderance of probability.
In criminal case, the guilt of the accused of the offences of rash and negligent act/driving is to be assessed and evaluated on the touch-stone of proof "beyond reasonable doubt", but in the claim proceedings, the evidences ought to be appreciated regarding the rash - 11 - and negligent driving of the drivers but not the offence.
Therefore, the degree of appreciation of evidence in criminal cases and in motor vehicles accident claim proceedings are entirely two different aspects.
Even though there is no requirement of strict Rules of pleadings and evidence in considering the claim petition arising out of motor vehicles accident cases.
But, the theory of preponderance of probability means upon evidence produced before the Tribunal/Court what would get impression in the mind regarding occurrence of incident is to be assessed.
But in criminal cases whether the named accused is guilty or not is to be assessed.
This is difference between the appreciation of evidence so far as rash and negligent aspect is concerned in both these category of cases.
Even though basically in both proceedings, the fundamental aspect regarding finding of rash and negligent aspect but in criminal cases, strictly it is to be tested and held whether the accused is guilty of offence of rash and negligent driving/act but in claim proceedings, whether due to rash and negligent driving/act, the - 12 - accident was caused or not is to be considered.
Therefore, where one of the prime aspect is to consider the rash and negligent aspect, the entirety of rash and negligence or contributory or composite negligence can be considered.
Therefore,
when the claim petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, the rash and negligent aspect is to be considered in its entirety.
Section 165 of Motor Vehicle Act stipulates constitution of Claim Tribunal and an application is to be filed before the Claim Tribunal.
The Tribunal while giving this finding on the theory of preponderance of probabilities as arraigned of parties is not the factual truth to hold that the charge sheeted driver always and alone is responsible for the accident where the theory beyond reasonable doubt is not applicable and where the case is to be considered on the theory of preponderance of probabilities.
The human mind gets impression as to whether the accident or incident has happened or not and who is responsible and to what extent, without going in depth in considering the evidence applying any strict rules.
Based upon the evidence produced before the Tribunal what is emerged to get - 15 - impression about occurrence of incident or accident and to what proportion the persons are responsible is the preponderance of probabilities.
The application of strict rules of evidence and theory of beyond reasonable doubt is applicable where a person is prosecuted for guilty of certain offence.
Considering the guilty of offence and responsible in causing incident or accident is different.
In the claim proceedings, the Tribunal/Court is not an obligation to find the guilty of a person for commission of offence rather the claim petition ought to be considered on the theory of preponderance of probabilities to get impression as to what must have been occurred upon the impression got by the evidence on record.
Therefore, the theory of preponderance of probabilities is applicable to ascertain whether any incident or accident has occurred or not and who is responsible and to what extent.
It cannot be said that the driver of the autorickshaw was not at all rash and negligent.
If the driver of the autorickshaw had seen the deceased was coming on the wrong side and the driver of the autorickshaw could have slowed down the speed of the vehicle
Therefore, these factors are considered and there is contributory negligence on the part of both the drivers of the vehicles.
Therefore, it is proved that the deceased while riding TVS Scooty and the driver of the autorickshaw both have contributed rashness and negligence while causing the accident.
Therefore, whether it is - 21 - proved that the deceased has also contributed negligence towards the accident and also the driver of the autorickshaw had also contributed negligence and where it is found that both are responsible,
then 25% of contributory negligence can be attributed on the part of the deceased and 75% can be attributed on the part of the driver of the autorickshaw.
Simply recording the documents and without making discussion on it and coming to the conclusion is not an application of mind.
An application of mind while appreciating the evidence on record is to referring and considering the documents and discussion on the contents therein along with oral evidence and application of mind is an appreciation of evidence on its touchstone on the principle as above discussed.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v.
Nanu Ram & Others3, each legal dependents are entitled to Rs.40,000/- with 10% escalation.

(2017) 16 SCC 680 - 25 - Rs.10,619/- + Rs.2,655/- (25% of Rs.10,619/-) =Rs.13,274/- Rs.13,274/- x  x 14 x 12=Rs.16,72,524/-
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.16,72,524/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
19. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of love and affection and Rs.40,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
There are four legal dependents.
Hence, compensation of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 4 + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head loss of consortium including loss of love and affection.
